\leanok
\uses{Complexity.satAppendCfg, Complexity.satAppendTM, Complexity.satStreamPos, Complexity.satStreamPos_read, Complexity.satStreamPos_succ, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_append, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{5}
Let $x$, $w$, and $r$ be Boolean words, and suppose $x=p r$ for a Boolean word $p$,
where juxtaposition denotes concatenation. Starting in the appender's copy state with
input head at the clamped position corresponding to $|p|$, work tape holding $w p$, and
work head at position $|w p|$, after exactly $|r|+1$ steps the machine is in its copy
state with input head at the clamped position corresponding to $|x|$, work tape holding
$w x$, and work head at position $|w x|-1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Rewinding the work tape]
\lean{Complexity.satAppend_rewind}
\label{Complexity.satAppend_rewind}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.satAppendCfg, Complexity.satAppendTM, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_nat, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x$ and $w$ be Boolean words and let $i$ be a valid input-head position for input
$x$. For every integer $r$ with $r\le |w|$, starting in the appender's work-rewind state
with input head at $i$, work tape holding $w$, and work head at $r-1$, after exactly
$r+1$ steps the machine is in its input-rewind state with input head still at $i$, work
tape still holding $w$, and work head at zero.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[First halt in a padded run]
\lean{Complexity.sat_call_first_halt}
\label{Complexity.sat_call_first_halt}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.Halted, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_of_halt, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine, let $x$ be a finite binary input,
and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on $x$. If $c$ is not halted and the run from $c$
is halted after $t$ steps, then there is a time $u$ with $0<u\le t$ such that the run is
not halted at any time $v<u$, and the configuration at time $u$ equals the configuration
at time $t$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Clean return of the appender]
\lean{Complexity.satAppend_clean}
\label{Complexity.satAppend_clean}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.satAppendCfg, Complexity.satAppendTM, Complexity.satAppend_copy, Complexity.satAppend_rewind, Complexity.satAppend_seek, Complexity.satStreamPos, Complexity.sat_call_first_halt, Turing.Cfg.Halted, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM.timed_rewind, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{5}
For every pair of Boolean words $x$ and $w$, there is a positive integer time $t$ with
$t \le 2|w|+3|x|+6$ such that the appender, started on input $x$ with its work tape
holding $w$ in the standard one-tape word assignment, is not halted at any time $v<t$,
and at time $t$ is halted in exactly the configuration whose work tape holds $w$
followed by $x$, with the input head at its initial position, the work head at zero, and
the output empty.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Padded action]
\lean{Complexity.satPadAction}
\label{Complexity.satPadAction}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action}
The embedding of an action over $k$ work tapes into an action over $K \ge k$
work tapes: the extra tapes are neither written nor moved.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Padded machine]
\lean{Complexity.satPadTM}
\label{Complexity.satPadTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.satPadAction, Turing.FinTM}
The embedding of a finite machine with $k$ work tapes into one with $K \ge k$
work tapes by padding every transition; all modules of the streaming host share
tape zero, with each source bank padded on the right.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Padded configuration]
\lean{Complexity.satPadCfg}
\label{Complexity.satPadCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg}
The embedding of a configuration over $k$ work tapes into one over $K \ge k$
work tapes: the padding tapes are genuinely blank with heads at the origin.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Padding commutes with an action]
\lean{Complexity.satPad_apply}
\label{Complexity.satPad_apply}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.satPadAction, Complexity.satPadCfg, Turing.Action, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg}
\difficulty{3}
Let $k$ and $K$ be natural numbers, let $S$ be a set of states, and let $x$ be a finite
Boolean input word. For every action $a$ on $k$ work tapes and configuration $c$ on
those tapes with input $x$, applying the action padded to $K$ tapes to the configuration
padded to $K$ tapes gives the same configuration as padding to $K$ tapes the result of
applying $a$ to $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Padding commutes with machine runs]
\lean{Complexity.satPad_run}
\label{Complexity.satPad_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.satPadAction, Complexity.satPadCfg, Complexity.satPadTM, Complexity.satPad_apply, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_comm_of_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with $k$ work tapes, and
let $K\ge k$. For every Boolean input word, every configuration $c$ of $M$ on that
input, and every $t\in\mathbb{N}$, running the machine padded to $K$ work tapes for $t$
steps from the padded configuration equals the padding to $K$ tapes of the $t$-step run
of $M$ from $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Padding canonical seam configurations]
\lean{Complexity.satPad_seam}
\label{Complexity.satPad_seam}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.satPadCfg, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{3}
Let $k,K$ be natural numbers with $0<k$, let $S$ be a state type, let $x$ be a Boolean
input word, and let $q\in S$ and $w,o$ be Boolean words. Padding the configuration on
$x$ formed from state $q$ and the tape-word assignment that places $w$ on tape $0$ and
leaves the other tapes empty, with output set to $o$, to $K$ work tapes gives the
configuration on $x$ formed from the same state and word assignment over $K$ tapes, with
output $o$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Call-stopping wrapper]
\lean{Complexity.satStopTM}
\label{Complexity.satStopTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction}
Given a machine $C$ with designated entry and exit states, the wrapper machine
whose states carry an additional Boolean release flag: it simulates $C$, raising
the flag after the first step, and halts silently as soon as the flag is raised
and the control is at the designated exit. The flag ensures that even an entry
equal to the exit executes at least once.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Release-flag embedding]
\lean{Complexity.satStopCfg}
\label{Complexity.satStopCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg}
The embedding of a configuration of a machine into the call-stopping wrapper
with a given release-flag value; all physical fields (tapes, heads, output) are
preserved.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Step of the call-stopping wrapper]
\lean{Complexity.satStop_step}
\label{Complexity.satStop_step}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.satStopCfg, Complexity.satStopTM, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{3}
Let $C$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, with designated states
$\mathrm{entry}$ and $\mathrm{exit}$. For a Boolean input word $x$, a configuration $c$
of $C$ on $x$, and a flag $b\in\{0,1\}$, suppose that $c$ is live and that $c$ is not in
state $\mathrm{exit}$ whenever $b=1$. One step of the wrapper machine, from the
configuration formed by adjoining flag $b$ to $c$, yields the configuration formed by
adjoining flag $1$ to the result of one step of $C$ from $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Liveness of run prefixes]
\lean{Complexity.sat_live_prefix}
\label{Complexity.sat_live_prefix}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_of_halt}
\difficulty{3}
Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$, let $S$ be a state type, let $x$ be a binary string, let $M$ be a
$k$-work-tape Turing machine over the binary alphabet with states in $S$, and let $c$ be
a configuration on input $x$. If the machine has not halted after $t$ steps from $c$,
then it has not halted after any $u\le t$ steps from $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Halting After a Clean Call]
\lean{Complexity.satStop_clean}
\label{Complexity.satStop_clean}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.satStopCfg, Complexity.satStopTM, Complexity.satStop_step, Complexity.sat_live_prefix, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{5}
Let $C$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, with designated entry and
exit states, and let $x$, $\mathrm{arg}$, $\mathrm{result}$, and $\mathrm{out}$ be
Boolean words. Starting from the configuration on input $x$ with entry state and tape
contents given by the state word of $\mathrm{arg}$, suppose $t>0$, the machine's state
is not the exit state at any time $v$ with $0<v<t$, and at time $t$ it is in the
configuration with exit state, tape contents given by the state word of
$\mathrm{result}$, and output $\mathrm{out}$. Then the call-stopping wrapper, started on
input $x$ with release flag down, entry state, and tape contents given by the state word
of $\mathrm{arg}$, reaches after $t+1$ steps a halted configuration with release flag
raised, exit state, tape contents given by the state word of $\mathrm{result}$, and
output $\mathrm{out}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Host state space]
\lean{Complexity.SatHostState}
\label{Complexity.SatHostState}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM}
The control-state space of the streaming host: a single anchor state plus the
disjoint union of the state spaces of six finite modules (startup append and
install, then the recurring pack, append, emit, and install calls).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Module return successor]
\lean{Complexity.satHostNext}
\label{Complexity.satHostNext}
\leanok
The return destination of each of the six modules: the startup appender
continues to the startup installer, and the pack, append, and emit calls
continue to the next module; the two installers return to the unique loop
anchor.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Module entry state]
\lean{Complexity.satHostEntry}
\label{Complexity.satHostEntry}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SatHostState, Turing.FinTM}
Given six finite modules and an index $i \in \{0, \dots, 5\}$, the entry state of
module $i$ is the host control state corresponding to the initial state of the
$i$-th module inside the finite body.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Module return state]
\lean{Complexity.satHostRet}
\label{Complexity.satHostRet}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SatHostState, Complexity.satHostEntry, Complexity.satHostNext, Turing.FinTM}
The host control state to which the $i$-th module returns: the entry of its
successor module, or the loop anchor when there is none. No additional tape
operation is performed on return.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[The streaming host machine]
\lean{Complexity.satHostTM}
\label{Complexity.satHostTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SatHostState, Complexity.satHostEntry, Complexity.satHostRet, Complexity.satPadTM, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.emitAction}
The finite controller hosting the six modules on one shared padded work bank:
the anchor dispatches into the recurring call sequence, and inside a module
every transition (including the halting one) is forwarded by the
output-emitting embedding, redirecting halts to the module's return state. The
clean-call contracts restore the shared scratch before each next call.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Forwarded padded seam configuration]
\lean{Complexity.satHost_seam}
\label{Complexity.satHost_seam}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SatHostState, Complexity.satHostRet, Complexity.satPadCfg, Complexity.satPad_seam, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.emitCfg, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a family of six finite Boolean Turing machines, let $K\in\mathbb{N}$, and let
$i\in\{0,1,2,3,4,5\}$ index a machine with positive work-tape count. For Boolean words
$x,w,\mathrm{pre},\mathrm{out}$, a state $q$ of machine $i$, and an optional state $s$
of that machine, forwarding the configuration on input $x$ with optional state $s$,
work-tape word $w$ on tape $0$ and all other work tapes blank, and output
$\mathrm{out}$—padded to $K$ work tapes—gives the configuration on input $x$ with
optional state mapped into the host state space (or the return state of module $i$ if
$s$ is absent), work-tape word $w$ on tape $0$ and all other work tapes blank, and
output $\mathrm{pre}\,\mathrm{out}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Running a Module in the Host]
\lean{Complexity.satHost_call}
\label{Complexity.satHost_call}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SatHostState, Complexity.satHostEntry, Complexity.satHostRet, Complexity.satHostTM, Complexity.satHost_seam, Complexity.satPadCfg, Complexity.satPadTM, Complexity.satPad_run, Turing.Cfg.Halted, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.emitCfg, Turing.emit_run, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{5}
Let six finite Boolean Turing machines be given, padded to a common work-tape count $K$;
choose a module index $i\in\{0,1,2,3,4,5\}$ whose machine has positive work-tape count.
Let $x,\mathrm{arg},\mathrm{result},\mathrm{out},\mathrm{pre}$ be Boolean words and $q$
a state of module $i$. Suppose the module started on input $x$ at its entry
configuration with argument word on tape zero and all other tapes blank stays unhalted
at every time $v<t$, and at time $t$ reaches its halted configuration with state
component absent, tape zero holding $\mathrm{result}$, all other tapes blank, and output
$\mathrm{out}$. Then the host started at module $i$'s entry on input $x$, with the same
argument word and output prefix $\mathrm{pre}$, never reaches the loop-anchor state at
any time $v<t$; at time $t$ it is in module $i$'s return state with tape zero holding
$\mathrm{result}$, all other tapes blank, and output $\mathrm{pre}\,\mathrm{out}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Joining guarded run segments]
\lean{Complexity.sat_guard_add}
\label{Complexity.sat_guard_add}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add}
\difficulty{3}
Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$, let $S$ be a state type, let $x$ be a binary string, let $M$ be a
$k$-work-tape Turing machine over the binary alphabet with states in $S$, let $q\in S$,
and let $c,d$ be configurations on input $x$. For $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$, suppose the state
at every time $v<a$ in the run from $c$ is different from $q$, the run from $c$ reaches
configuration $d$ at time $a$, and the state at every time $v<b$ in the run from $d$ is
different from $q$. Then the state at every time $v<a+b$ in the run from $c$ is
different from $q$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Clean-module contract]
\lean{Complexity.SatClean}
\label{Complexity.SatClean}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.Halted, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.stateWord}
The uniform contract for a host module $M$ with result and emission functions
and a budget $B$: $M$ has a positive tape count, and for every native input and
argument word there is a positive time within $B$ of the argument length at
which $M$, started at its entry over the state word of the argument, first halts
— in the canonical configuration over the state word of the result, having
emitted exactly the prescribed chunk, with the native input untouched.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Stopping wrapper for a bridge computation]
\lean{Complexity.satClean_stop}
\label{Complexity.satClean_stop}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SatClean, Complexity.satStopTM, Complexity.satStop_clean, Complexity.sat_call_first_halt, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{4}
Let $C$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, with a positive number of
work tapes and designated states $e_0$ and $e_1$. Let $r$ and $s$ map Boolean words to
Boolean words, and let $B$ map natural numbers to natural numbers. Suppose that for
every Boolean input $x$ and argument $a$, there is a time $t$ with $0<t\le B(|a|)$ such
that, at every positive time $v<t$, the run of $C$ on input $x$, started in state $e_0$
with $a$ on the first work tape and all other work tapes blank, is not in state $e_1$;
at time $t$ its configuration is the canonical configuration in state $e_1$ with $r(a)$
on the first work tape, all other work tapes blank, and output $s(a)$. Then the wrapper
that simulates $C$ and halts silently upon reaching $e_1$ after at least one step
satisfies the clean-module contract with result function $r$, emission function $s$, and
budget $n\mapsto B(n)+1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Polynomial bridge bound]
\lean{Complexity.sat_bridge_bound}
\label{Complexity.sat_bridge_bound}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For all natural numbers $c,A,d,n,\mathrm{len}$ satisfying $\mathrm{len}\le A(n+1)^d$,
one has
\[
c\bigl(A(n+1)^d+n+\mathrm{len}+1\bigr)+1\le \bigl(c(2A+1)+1\bigr)(n+1)^{d+1}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Polynomial-time clean installation]
\lean{Complexity.satClean_install}
\label{Complexity.satClean_install}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.SatClean, Complexity.satClean_stop, Complexity.satStopTM, Complexity.sat_bridge_bound, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.FinTM.exists_installCallTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.output_length_le}
\difficulty{4}
For every polynomial-time computable function $f$ from Boolean words to Boolean words,
there exist a finite Turing machine $M$ and natural numbers $A,d$ such that $M$ has at
least one work tape and, for every Boolean input word $x$ and argument word $z$, there
is a positive time $t\le A(|z|+1)^d$ at which the run from the initial state with $z$ on
the first work tape and all other work tapes blank first halts. At that time its
configuration has $f(z)$ on the first work tape, all other work tapes blank, and empty
output; the input head and work-tape heads and contents are those of the canonical
starting configuration, apart from the first tape now containing $f(z)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Polynomial-time clean emission]
\lean{Complexity.satClean_emit}
\label{Complexity.satClean_emit}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.SatClean, Complexity.satClean_stop, Complexity.satStopTM, Complexity.sat_bridge_bound, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.FinTM.exists_emitCallTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.output_length_le}
\difficulty{4}
For every polynomial-time computable function $f$ from Boolean words to Boolean words,
there exist a finite Turing machine $M$ and natural numbers $A,d$ such that $M$ has at
least one work tape and, for every Boolean input word $x$ and argument word $z$, there
is a positive time $t\le A(|z|+1)^d$ at which the run from the initial state with $z$ on
the first work tape and all other work tapes blank first halts. At that time its
configuration has $f(z)$ on the first work tape, all other work tapes blank, and output
exactly $f(z)$; the input head and work-tape heads and contents are those of the
canonical starting configuration, apart from the first tape now containing $f(z)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Length of a pair encoding]
\lean{Complexity.satPair_length}
\label{Complexity.satPair_length}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{2}
For all Boolean words $u$ and $v$, the pair encoding of $u$ and $v$ has length
$2|u|+|v|+2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Request Budget Inequality]
\lean{Complexity.sat_request_budget}
\label{Complexity.sat_request_budget}
\leanok
\difficulty{2}
Let $A,d,D,n,m$ be natural numbers with $d \le D$ and $m+1 \le 32(n+1)$. Then $A(m+1)^d
\le A\bigl(32(n+1)\bigr)^D$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Clean Module at a Host Call Site]
\lean{Complexity.satHost_clean}
\label{Complexity.satHost_clean}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SatClean, Complexity.satHostEntry, Complexity.satHostRet, Complexity.satHostTM, Complexity.satHost_call, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{2}
Let six finite Boolean Turing machines be given, padded to a common work-tape count $K$,
and let $i\in\{0,1,2,3,4,5\}$. Suppose module $i$ satisfies the clean-module contract
with result function $f$, emission function $g$, and budget $B$. For every Boolean input
$x$, argument word $\mathrm{arg}$, and output prefix $\mathrm{pre}$, there is a positive
time $t\le B(|\mathrm{arg}|)$ such that the host, started at module $i$'s entry on $x$
with $\mathrm{arg}$ on tape zero, all other tapes blank, and output prefix
$\mathrm{pre}$, does not reach the loop-anchor state at any time before $t$, and at time
$t$ is in the module's return state with $f(\mathrm{arg})$ on tape zero, all other tapes
blank, and output $\mathrm{pre}\,g(\mathrm{arg})$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Polynomial-Time Computability of the Reduction]
\lean{Complexity.satReduction_poly}

\leanok

\begin{theorem}[SAT reduces to 3SAT]
\lean{Complexity.SAT_reducible_SAT3}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p196-b010}
\label{Complexity.SAT_reducible_SAT3}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SAT, Complexity.SAT3, Complexity.satReduction, Complexity.satReduction_correct, Complexity.satReduction_poly}
\difficulty{1}
$\mathrm{SAT} \le_p \mathrm{3SAT}$: there is a polynomial-time computable map on
binary strings — clause splitting with fresh variables — under which membership
in $\mathrm{SAT}$ of any string is equivalent to membership in $\mathrm{3SAT}$
of its image. [AB09, Lemma~2.14]
\end{theorem}
